summary: Ashgrove Labs passes Point 1: it is outperforming its industrial robotics benchmark, showing consistent positive YoY revenue growth and an active product launch cadence that supports multi-year sales potential. It fails Point 4 because a customer describes the sales team as transactional price-sheet senders rather than consultative advisors. It fails Point 7 because current and former employees cite chronic excessive overtime, low pay, and high turnover.

Point 1 passes: Aurel Systems outperforms its packaging machinery benchmark with 18.3% two-year growth versus 11.5%, recent quarterly revenue remains positive, and it continues launching new commercialized products. Point 4 fails because customer feedback indicates a transactional price-list sales approach rather than consultative selling. Point 7 fails due to evidence of chronic overtime and high employee turnover.

Bramble Labs outperforms its water treatment equipment peer benchmark with 21.1% two-year growth versus 14.8%, and recent quarters show consistently positive year-over-year revenue growth. Product launches, including the BR-420 and BR-540, support ongoing market expansion. Customer and employee interviews also indicate a technically consultative sales organization and strong labor relations with fair pay and low turnover.

Point 1 fails because Cobalt Holdings underperformed its packaging machinery industry benchmark over the multi-year period, recent quarterly growth is uneven with a sharp YoY decline in 2025Q4, and product launch cadence has been limited after 2024Q4. Point 4 passes due to strong customer feedback on consultative, technically knowledgeable, and proactive sales support. Point 7 passes because both current and former employees report positive labor relations, low turnover, and fair treatment.

Copperfield Technologies shows strong multi-year market potential, with 27.9% two-year growth versus a 20.1% semiconductor equipment benchmark, consistently positive YoY quarterly revenue trends, and recent product launches. Customer feedback indicates a proactive, technically competent sales organization, while employee interviews point to positive labor relations and low turnover. All three Fisher framework points therefore pass.

Point 1 fails because Driftwood Systems underperforms its specialty chemicals peer benchmark over the multi-year period, with 8.6% growth versus 12.0%, and recent quarterly growth is uneven despite some product launches. Point 4 passes because customer feedback describes a proactive, technically knowledgeable, and consultative sales organization. Point 7 fails because both current and former employees report chronic overtime and severe turnover, indicating negative labor relations.

Dunmore Holdings passes Point 1 because its 23.0% two-year growth outperforms the 18.9% precision optics benchmark, quarterly YoY revenue growth remains consistently positive, and recent product launches support continued sales potential. Point 4 passes due to evidence of proactive, technically competent sales support, and Point 7 passes because employee interviews indicate low turnover, fair treatment, and healthy morale.

Elmstead Technologies outperforms its industrial robotics benchmark with 27.5% two-year growth versus 21.7%, and its quarterly revenue trajectory shows consistently positive YoY growth, supporting durable market potential. Its recent product launches and technically consultative sales organization further reinforce Fisher's growth and sales criteria. Labor relations also appear strong, with fair pay, high retention, and constructive problem resolution reported by both current and former employees.

Emberly Systems passes Point 1 because it is outpacing its precision optics benchmark with 26.2% two-year growth versus 18.9%, recent quarterly YoY growth remains consistently positive, and product launches continue. Point 4 passes due to strong customer feedback on proactive, technically knowledgeable account management. Point 7 passes because current and former employees describe fair pay, low turnover, and good morale.

Everline Dynamics passes Point 1 because its 19.0% two-year growth outperforms the 11.5% packaging machinery benchmark, recent YoY revenue growth remains positive, and product launches such as the EV-730 and EV-770 support ongoing commercial vitality. Point 4 passes based on a customer interview citing proactive, technically knowledgeable account management, and Point 7 passes due to positive employee and former-manager commentary on fair pay, low turnover, and responsive management.

Point 1 passes because Falcrest outperforms its industrial robotics benchmark, shows consistently positive year-over-year revenue growth in recent quarters, and continues launching new commercialized products. Point 4 fails due to a customer report that salespeople are transactional and provide little consultative support. Point 7 fails because employee interviews indicate low morale, pay-related strike risk, excessive overtime, and turnover.

Fernhill Group passes Point 1 because it outperforms its food ingredients industry benchmark with 14.4% two-year growth versus 9.8%, recent YoY growth is mostly positive, and recent product launches support commercial vitality. Point 4 fails because customer feedback indicates a transactional sales approach focused on price lists rather than consultative advice. Point 7 passes because current and former employees report good treatment, low turnover, and positive labor relations.

Granite Group passes Point 1 because it outperforms its medical devices industry benchmark, shows consistently positive recent quarterly revenue growth, and maintains an active product launch cadence. Point 4 passes on evidence of a consultative, technically knowledgeable account manager, while Point 7 passes given strong employee retention, positive morale, and favorable comments on pay and training.

Point 1 fails because Halcyon Works' 2-year revenue growth of 7.7% materially underperforms the specialty chemicals benchmark of 12.0%, signaling insufficient market-share momentum despite some positive recent quarterly comparisons and recent product launches. Point 4 passes because customer feedback describes a proactive, technically knowledgeable account manager with consultative engagement. Point 7 passes because both current and former employees report strong morale, high retention, fair pay, and good training.

Hollins Group passes Point 1: it outperforms its medical devices peer benchmark over the multi-year period, shows consistently positive YoY revenue growth in recent quarters, and has active commercialized product lines. It fails Point 4 because customer feedback indicates a transactional, price-list-only sales approach rather than consultative selling. It passes Point 7, with employee and former-manager interviews pointing to fair pay, low turnover, and healthy labor relations.

Ironbark Technologies fails Fisher Point 1 because its 2-year revenue growth of 14.4% lags the industrial robotics benchmark of 21.7%, indicating underperformance versus peers despite positive recent YoY growth and some product launches. Points 4 and 7 pass: customer interviews describe a consultative, technically knowledgeable, proactive sales organization, and employee interviews indicate fair treatment, low turnover, and healthy morale.

Point 1 fails because Juniper Industries' two-year growth of 14.5% trails the industrial robotics benchmark of 21.7%, and recent quarterly momentum is mixed with a YoY decline in 2025Q4 and only sparse product launches. Point 4 passes due to a customer report of proactive, technically supported sales engagement, and Point 7 passes because current and former employees describe fair treatment and very low turnover.

Kestrel Technologies fails Point 1 because it underperforms its food ingredients industry benchmark over the multi-year period, recent same-quarter sales growth is weak or negative, and product launch cadence has slowed materially since 2024Q2. Point 4 passes based on a customer report that the salesperson was proactive and brought an engineer to resolve a problem, indicating consultative technical support. Point 7 fails because both current and former employees describe chronic overtime and high monthly turnover, indicating poor labor relations.

Lindale Holdings passes Point 1: it outperforms the food ingredients benchmark with 13.6% two-year growth versus 9.8%, recent YoY growth is positive, and it has launched new plant-protein products in 2025. However, it fails Point 4 because a customer reports four sales contacts in two years and poor product knowledge, indicating weak sales organization. It also fails Point 7 due to chronic excessive overtime, monthly attrition, and employee complaints about pay and workload.

Point 1 passes because Northwind Group's 24.7% two-year growth outperforms the semiconductor-equipment benchmark of 20.1%, recent quarterly YoY growth is positive in the newest periods, and product launches remain active. Point 4 passes due to evidence of proactive, technically competent sales support, and Point 7 passes because current and former employees report fair pay, strong retention, and good training.
